_meta.description: U.S. EPA Air Quality Index (AQI) breakpoints for PM2.5 and PM10, in micrograms per cubic meter (24-hr average).
_meta.pm25_source: EPA 'Final Updates to the Air Quality Index (AQI) for Particulate Matter' fact sheet, effective 2024-05-06 (verified directly against the EPA PDF at publish time: https://www.epa.gov/system/files/documents/2024-02/pm-naaqs-air-quality-index-fact-sheet.pdf). This superseded the 2012 breakpoints.
_meta.pm10_source: EPA 40 CFR Part 58, Appendix G (long-standing PM10 breakpoints; PM10 NAAQS was not revised by the 2024 PM2.5 rule).
_meta.verify_at: https://www.airnow.gov/aqi/aqi-basics/ — always cross-check against AirNow for the authoritative, current table.

pm25.guidance: Air quality is good. No action needed.
Acceptable for most people. Unusually sensitive individuals may consider limiting prolonged outdoor exertion.
People with heart/lung disease, older adults, children, and pregnant people should reduce prolonged/heavy outdoor exertion.
Everyone may begin to experience effects. Sensitive groups should avoid prolonged outdoor exertion; consider an indoor HEPA purifier.
Health alert. Everyone should reduce outdoor exertion; keep windows closed and run air purification if available.
Health emergency conditions. Stay indoors with filtered air; follow local public health guidance.
